en: The letter *a* is Vāsudeva, and the letter *ā* is the Grandfather (Brahmā);
the letter *ā* is also proclaimed for purposes of worship and as an auspicious sign. The letter *i* is said to be Kāma, and the letter *rī* is said to be Lakṣmī.
The letter *u* is said to be Śaṅkara, and the letter *ū* is also for protection.
The letter *ṛ* is the mother of the gods, and the letter *ṝ* is the progenitor of the Danujas.
The letter *ḷ* is the source of the gods, while *ḹ* is called the mother by the virtuous.
The letter *e* is said to be Viṣṇu, and the letter *ai* is Maheśvara;
the letter *o* is Brahmā, while the letter *au* is called Rudra.
The syllable *aṃ* is the Supreme Brahman, and the syllable *aḥ* is the Lord Maheśvara.

Who is designated as Prajāpati, and who is called Vāyu? Who is declared to be the Ātman, and what is cited as the Light? What is said to be the head, and what is proclaimed as Water? And what is celebrated as Bliss?
On earth, *ku* is well-known; in the sense of contempt, *ku* is proclaimed.
*Kha* is declared to be a sense organ; *kha* is cited as space.
*Kha* is well-known in the sense of heaven; *kha* is proclaimed in the sense of a serpent.
Likewise, they say that *kha* refers to a chasm, and *kha* is proclaimed to mean "void.
*Go* is designated as Gaṇapati, and *go* is proclaimed to be Gandharva.
*Gaṃ* is song (*gīta*), *gā* is a verse (*gāthā*), *gauḥ* is a cow (*dhenur*), and *gauḥ* is Sarasvatī.
The syllable *ga* is designated as "mother," and on earth it is proclaimed as "cow.
*Gha* is declared to be the "bell," and *ghā* is proclaimed as the "small bell" (*kiṅkiṇī*). *Ghā* is declared to be the "simile," and *ghu* is proclaimed as the "bad sound."
The letter *gha* is proclaimed as killing (*hanana*), and the letter *gha* is celebrated as striking (*gandhana*).

The letter *ṅa* is known as Bhairava, and the letter *ṅa* is remembered as the sense object (*viṣaya*). The letter *ca* is known as the Moon (*candramas*), and it is also celebrated as a thief (*taskara*).
The letter *cha* is declared to mean "pure," and *cha* is proclaimed to mean "crossing over.
The letter *cha* is also declared by learned scholars skilled in words to mean "cutting.
The letter *ja* is declared to mean "speed," and *ja* is proclaimed to mean "the buttocks."

The letter *ja* is declared by those renowned as experts in phonetics to signify "the conqueror" (*jetā*). The letter *jha* occurs in the sense of a whirlwind (*jhañjhāvāta*), and *jha* is also cited in the sense of "destroyed" (*naṣṭa*).
The letter *ña* is said to denote "singing" (*gāyana*), and the letter *ña* also denotes a gurgling sound (*ghargharadhvani*).
In the sound *ṭaṅkāra*, *ṭ* is proclaimed to be on earth; *ṭā* and *ṭo* are proclaimed to be in sound.
*Ṭha* is declared to be Maheśvara, and *ṭha* is proclaimed to be in the void.
*Ṭha* is also said to be in the great sound, as well as in the orb of the moon.
The letter *ḍa* is declared to be Śaṅkara, and it is proclaimed as the sound of terror.
The letter *ḍha* is proclaimed as the *ḍhakkā* drum, and also in the sound that is devoid of qualities (*nirguṇa*).
The letter *ṇa* is proclaimed in the sense of knowledge, and is also celebrated in the sense of ascertainment (*nirṇaya*).
The letter *ta* is said to be a thief; it is proclaimed to be in the chest and the tail.
The letter *tha* occurs on a mountain of stone; the letter *tha* is for protection from fear. *Daṃ* is declared to be a wife; *do* is in the verbal roots meaning "to give" and "to cut."

*Dha* is taught for wealth (*dhana*), the Lord of Wealth (*dhanesa*), and *Dhātṛ*; *dhā* is likewise shown. *Dhīṣaṇā* and *dhī* are fully explained as meaning intellect; *dhū* shall be used for burden and anxiety.
The letter *na* is proclaimed for the Sugata and for bondage; *nu* is celebrated in the sense of praise.

The letter *na* is declared to mean "leader" (*netṛ*) and "guide" (*nī*); it is celebrated as "boat" (*nau*) in the sense of crossing over. The syllable *na* is praised for the Buddha of the Sugatas and is also proclaimed for the Sun.
The word *na* is proclaimed for a welcome (*svāgata*), a kinsman (*bandhu*), a tree, and the Sun.
The letter *pa* is well-known as Kubera and is proclaimed to be in the west.

The letter *pa* is said to be in the wind (*pavana*), and *pā* is in drinking (*pāna*) and *pātṛ* (the drinker). The letter *pha* occurs in phlegm (*kapha*) and wind (*vāta*), and is likewise proclaimed in calling (*āhvāna*).
The syllable *pha* is proclaimed in the case of a gale and is also celebrated as a letter;
*phi* is likewise declared in the sense of anger and also for fruitless speech.
*Ba* is said to be in the region of the chest and is cited in the sense of a mace.
The wise have declared that *nakṣatra* means a lunar mansion (*bha*), while *bha* is also proclaimed to mean a bee. *Bhā* is light, *bhū* is the earth, and *bhī* is said by the wise to mean fear.
*Ma* is Śiva, the Moon, and Brahmā; *mā* is also proclaimed to be Lakṣmī.
